newsitem.title: FRANCE: Korean anger over Thomson seen waning eventually.
newsitem.headline: Korean anger over Thomson seen waning eventually.

text.p: South Korea's anger towards France will take time to ease but should not durably hurt relations between the two countries, a French presidential envoy said on Tuesday.
South Korea is upset over France's decision to cancel the planned sale of consumer electronics group Thomson Multimedia (TMM) to Daewoo Electronics.

"It will take some time because there have been a lot of emotions here," Jean-Claude Paye, the former head of the OECD sent as a French envoy to Seoul to appease angered South Korean authorities, told RFI radio on Tuesday.
"You cannot have the feeling of being humiliated without reacting passionately, especially when there are some people who have interest in fanning the fire," he said.
"There is nevertheless a common interest to develop our partnership which goes back many years," Paye said.
South Korean President Kim Young-sam on Tuesday blasted a French decision to scuttle the sale of TMM to Daewoo as discriminatory, saying France could not be trusted.
"The South Korean people believe we have been totally discriminated against," Kim told the French presidential envoy.
"We have a bad impression of France and have come to think France cannot be trusted," he told Jean-Claude Paye in unusually blunt language.
Many South Koreans regard the snub to Daewoo, which had offered to buy the consumer electronics division of state-owned Thomson SA, as an act of overt racism.

"We hear the privatisation is being reviewed. It would be fortunate if the result is satisfactory otherwise there will be a major impact on Korean-French relations," Kim was quoted as saying in a statement.

Paye said on RFI that he had told South Korea that Daewoo could renew its candidacy for Thomson Multimedia. He also said he had been charged with transmitting a personal message from Kim to President Jacques Chirac, but he declined to disclose the content of the message.
Kim gave no indication there would be any immediate repercussions for French business contracts.
But he made a jibe about an Anglo-French high-speed railway system, the Train a Grande Vitesse (TGV), that South Korea has bought, being affected by the recent cold weather in France.

The French government is expected to relaunch the privatisation of Thomson SA before the end of January. It is expected to sell its 60 percent stake in defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF in 1997 but hold on to the currently loss-making TMM until 1998.
France in October decided to sell Thomson SA to Lagardere Groupe for one franc after an 11 billion francs ($2 billion) capital increase.
Lagardere would have sold TMM to Daewoo but the independent Privatisation Commission objected to the terms of the sale and the government suspended the privatisation in early December.
